objective: Construct and justify equivalent fractions by repartitioning the same whole, and distinguish equal fraction values from equal quantities when wholes differ.
conceptual_invariants: Equivalent fractions name the same point or same proportion of one fixed whole.
Splitting every existing part into the same number of equal subparts changes the fraction name but not the represented amount.
Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero whole number preserves the fraction value.
Equal fraction values do not guarantee equal physical quantities when the wholes have different sizes.

learning_sequence.learner_action: Overlay two equal-length paper strips showing 1/2 and 2/4. Describe what stays unchanged and what changes.
Before repartitioning, predict the new numerator and denominator when every part is split into the same number of subparts, and predict whether the shaded length moves.
Repartition each part of one fixed whole by a chosen factor, align the before/after bars, and inspect the nonvisual fraction table.
Connect the unchanged shaded amount to multiplying numerator and denominator by the same factor; explain why adding the same amount does not preserve the value.
Complete a missing equivalent numerator, reject an add-both claim with a counterexample, and match an area model to a number-line point.
Use the recorded response pattern to enter exactly one misconception branch, complete its probe, and pass a different exit check before scaffolds fade.
Compare equivalent colored fractions on ribbons of different total lengths; decide separately whether the fractions are equivalent and whether the colored lengths are equal.
Complete server-controlled unseen repartition, counterexample and different-whole tasks with no bars, hints, worked steps or answer fields in the public payload.

diagnostic_router.observed_evidence: Learner accepts n/d=(n+1)/(d+1) or produces the add-both fraction.
diagnostic_router.probe: Compare 1/2 and 2/3 on equal bars and by exact cross-products.
socratic_path: Did every original part split into the same number of subparts?
Which multiplication changes 1/2 into the proposed fraction?
Can both fractions occupy the same point on one number line?
diagnostic_router.repair: Repartition one bar multiplicatively and contrast it with the add-both bar.
diagnostic_router.exit_check: Decide whether 2/5 and 3/6 are equivalent and give one invariant-based reason.

diagnostic_router.observed_evidence: Learner judges the larger denominator as the larger fraction without holding the whole fixed.
diagnostic_router.probe: Compare one fourth and one eighth cut from equal-length strips.
socratic_path: Are both wholes the same length?
What happens to one piece when the same whole has more equal parts?
Which piece covers more of the fixed whole?
diagnostic_router.repair: Align unit-fraction pieces on the same whole and announce their lengths nonvisually.
diagnostic_router.exit_check: Order 1/3 and 1/6 using a fixed whole and explain the denominator's role.

diagnostic_router.observed_evidence: Learner concludes equal fraction names always represent equal physical quantities.
diagnostic_router.probe: Compare one half of a 12-unit strip with one half of an 18-unit strip.
socratic_path: Are the fractions of each whole equal?
Are the wholes themselves equal in size?
What are the two actual shaded lengths?
diagnostic_router.repair: Record fraction value and quantity in separate table columns before comparing.
diagnostic_router.exit_check: Explain why 3/6 of 20 and 4/8 of 12 have equal fraction values but unequal quantities.

unseen_transfer_contract.requires_explanation: Name the fixed-whole condition and compute both represented quantities.

mve_reuse_contract.reused_capability: Keyboard-operable bounded shading of one fixed-denominator fraction bar with a live text status.
mve_reuse_contract.missing_capability: Paired equal-whole bars, repartition-by-factor, alignment comparison, and separate fraction-value versus quantity table.
mve_reuse_contract.assessment_rule: The guided component must remain absent from independent assessment.

accessibility_contract.keyboard_only: Choose a bar, choose repartition factor, repartition, align, compare and submit using native controls without dragging.
accessibility_contract.screen_reader_state: Announce whole identifier and length, numerator, denominator, repartition factor, shaded proportion and represented quantity after each change.
accessibility_contract.nonvisual_equivalent: A table exposes whole length, fraction, equivalent name and represented quantity for each bar.
accessibility_contract.focus_recovery: Rejected repartition keeps work and returns focus to the invalid factor with a concise reason.
accessibility_contract.reduced_motion: Use discrete before/after bar states and optional alignment outlines; no required animation.
